one_month_reasoning: No Salesforce earnings fall in the window: Q3 FY27 results historically land in early December (Q2 was Aug 26, Q1 May 27) [1]. In-window items are second-order: final settlement of the $25B ASR (expected October; retires more shares, already known) [1], closing of the Contentful (~$1.5B) and Fin (~$3.6B) deals (in guidance) [3], the late-October FOMC and peer software prints (ServiceNow, Microsoft) that can move the group. The stock has pulled back from ~$268 intramonth high to $231 after a +55% three-month run [15][4], so there are opposing short-horizon forces (post-earnings drift and momentum vs reversal after a sharp rally) that I treat as roughly cancelling. I therefore centre on today's price (median ~$232) with a monthly log-sd of ~12%, a little below 47%/3.5 = 13.4% because no earnings jump is scheduled; CRM's own historical monthly sd is ~10-11% [4]. Round 2: the supervisor confirmed the price path (intraday high $268.27 on 2026-09-03, close $225.31 on 9/29). The only new Item 5.02 8-K since then (2026-09-04) is a deferred-comp plan, not an officer change, so there is no new in-window event and the 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: Blend of 14.5x P/E on Sep-2027 NTM core EPS of ~$17.2 (1/3 FY28 $16.1 + 2/3 FY29 $17.8 = $250, 60%) and a 6.5% SBC-adjusted FCF yield on ~$16.3/share NTM owner FCF over ~787M post-ASR shares ($250, 40%) gives ~$250 twelve months out.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus ~$16.0 (MarketScreener); nudged +$0.1 toward a bottom-up build (FY27 core ~$13.7 x 838M = ~$11.5B net income, +~10-11%, over ~787M post-ASR shares = ~$16.1-16.3). ASR interest is already in the Q2/Q3 run-rate, and the ASR share reduction is fully in FY28.

FY28 $16.1 x ~1.105: ~9% net income growth (organic ~7-8% ex Informatica per Q3 guide, plus Contentful/Fin, flat ~34% margin) plus ~1.5% net open-market buybacks after SBC. No further ASR benefit counted, which fixes the round-1 double count (was x1.12 to ~$18.0).

Today ~14.4-14.5x forward (GuruFocus); June-2026 trough ~10x; peers WDAY ~11x, NOW ~24x; S&P software & services ~22x. Mature-software comparison set (ORCL/ADBE, 2007-2026) earned ~+9%/yr median-to-mean with no rerating needed. With organic growth only ~7-8% I no longer assume a re-rating above today's multiple (round 1 used 15x).

10-Q Note 9: $25B ASR, 103M initial shares at $198.34 (~80%), final settlement in Q3 FY27. At the ~$182 expected average price, $25B buys ~137M shares, so ~34M more arrive in October: 821M Q2 diluted less 34M = ~787M (round 1 used a rounder 800M).

Between the trough-level ~9% (June 2026) and ~4-5% at sector-average multiples. With ~$28B net debt (~$39.3B debt vs $11.4B cash [1]) plus ~$5.1B of cash for the Contentful and Fin deals [3], I use a higher-than-sector yield. Interest on the ASR notes is already in the FCF run-rate.

bear.story: AI-seat compression fears return (the H1-2026 derating took the stock down ~41%), or the H2 organic reacceleration fails at the Q3/Q4 prints (organic growth ~7-8% today). Engineering leadership is in transition after the 2026-08 departure. A 2027 recession (Kalshi ~20-39% over Aug-Sep 2026) would compound this. FY29 EPS ~$15.5 at ~10x, near the June-2026 trough. Mature-software analogs lost 30-52% in the 2022 derating and 42-67% peak-to-trough in 2008.

base.story: cRPO ~13-14%, organic growth creeps up from ~7-8% toward ~9%, margins ~34%, ongoing buybacks ~1.5%/yr; ~14.5x on ~$17.2 NTM core EPS. This matches the mature-software base rate of ~+8-9%/yr.

bull.story: Agentforce/Data 360 drives a visible organic reacceleration toward double digits; the software sector re-rates and CRM earns ~18.5x on ~$17.5 NTM EPS.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$160 CRM would trade at ~9x Sep-2027 NTM core EPS of ~$17.2, back near the June-2026 AI-panic low ($146). Reaching it most likely means cRPO growth has rolled over or guidance was cut, i.e. the promised H2 organic reacceleration failed (organic is ~7-8% ex Informatica), perhaps compounded by execution slippage under the new engineering leadership. It would not be ordinary 47%-vol noise. It is ~31% below spot, beyond the ~13% frequency of a >25% 12m drop in mature-software analogs.

Earnings quality: FY27 EPS includes ~$2.98/share of strategic-investment gains
reasoning: Facts: the FY27 guide is revenue $46.1-46.4B (+11-12%, of which slightly >4pts is Informatica, so organic is ~7-8%), a 34.3% non-GAAP margin and $16.67-16.71 non-GAAP EPS. That EPS includes $2.98 of H1 investment gains, so core is ~$13.7 [1]. After the ASR settles, diluted shares are ~787M [3]. FY28 is ~$16.1 (consensus ~$16.0 [6]), and FY29 is ~$17.8 on ~9% net income growth plus ~1.5% net buybacks, with no second ASR benefit. NTM core EPS at Sep-2027 is therefore ~$17.2. At $231 the stock is on ~14.4x forward [7]. Base rates: CRM's own 20-year history (12m log mean +16%, sd 33%) comes from its hyper-growth era, so I now anchor explicitly on a mature-software comparison set [17]. Pooled ORCL and ADBE Sep-to-Sep 12m log returns, 2007-2026 (n=38): mean +9.4%, median +8%, sd 33%, P(up) 71%, P(<-25%) 13%, P(>+35%) 24%. IGV (n=16): mean +15%, sd 21%. Stress analogs: 2008 peak-to-trough ORCL -42% and ADBE -67%; the non-recession 2022 derating was IGV -37% and ADBE -52%. Macro: I dropped the thin Polymarket input (~$9.6K volume). The deeper Kalshi 'Recession in 2027' contract (~$528K volume [11]) traded 38-39% on 2026-08-04 [20] and ~20% in late September per Kalshi's own post [21], which I could only read in a search snippet. I treat ~25% as a rough weight that is already covered by the stress component; it does not push the tail out further. The engineering-president departure (8-K 2026-08-05 [18]; the 2026-09-04 8-K is only a deferred-comp plan [19]) adds a little bear weight but is orderly and already priced. Fair value: ~$250 (14.5x on $17.2 = $250; 6.5% owner-FCF yield on $16.3/share = $250), about +8%, in line with the mature-software median. Distribution: 80% lognormal (median $248, sd 0.30) plus 20% stress lognormal (median $185, sd 0.46). That gives a median of ~$238, P(>=231) of ~54%, P(>=162) of 86% and P(>=347) of 12%, slightly lower and tighter than round 1. My fair value ends up close to the supervisor's $251 because we both corrected the same inputs, not because I anchored on it. I keep the bull weight at 25% rather than trimming it: the mature-software set shows P(>+35%) ~24%, and CRM's vol is higher than that set's. No options or implied-volatility data used.
